Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)

Required findings: ≥6 months elapsed since the prior cervical decompression or fusion at the adjacent level

Symptoms must include BOTH: (a) clinically significant daily pain causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing) AND (b) unremitting radicular pain radiating to the shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam must demonstrate ANY of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor weakness (biceps/triceps), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, positive Spurling's maneuver, OR unremitting radicular pain without concordant objective findings

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics/NSAIDs/steroids/gabapentinoids for ≥6 weeks, provider‑directed exercise program for ≥6 weeks, epidural steroid injection or selective nerve root block at the same level, plain cervical spine X‑rays (including flexion/extension) and advanced imaging confirming successful decompression/fusion at the prior level, MRI/CT demonstrating neural compression at the requested adjacent level caused by herniated disc, synovial/arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder)

Nicotine‑free status verified by either never‑smoker declaration or abstinence from all tobacco/nicotine products for ≥6 weeks prior to surgery, documented with objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range

Symptoms must include ANY of: upper or lower extremity weakness, numbness or pain; fine motor dysfunction (e.g., difficulty buttoning, handwriting); gait disturbance; new‑onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; frequent falls

Physical exam must demonstrate ANY of: abnormal grip‑release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone/spasticity, clonus, myelopathic hand
MRI or CT must show findings concordant with the patient’s symptoms and exam and be caused by cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis at the adjacent level

Non-Indications: Less than six months since the prior cervical decompression or fusion at the adjacent level
Absence of both significant daily pain and unremitting radicular pain for the radiculopathy indication
Lack of any objective neurological deficit or positive physical‑exam finding when required
Failure to complete the minimum conservative therapy trial (≥6 weeks of at least two modalities) or lack of documented inadequate response
Imaging that does not demonstrate neural compression at the requested adjacent level or shows adequate decompression at the prior level only
Presence of unmanaged significant mental/behavioral health disorder
Active tobacco use without documented ≥6‑week cessation and objective cotinine verification
For radiculopathy: MRI/CT findings not attributable to herniated disc, cyst, stenosis, or osteophyte
Important criteria & exceptions: Objective cotinine testing must be performed using a validated laboratory method (serum, urine, or saliva) and reported as within normal limits; self‑reported abstinence alone is insufficient
Conservative therapy may be waived only if contraindicated (e.g., allergy to NSAIDs, inability to tolerate PT) and must be documented with a justification note
Plain cervical spine X‑rays must include flexion and extension lateral views to confirm stability of the prior fusion
Only adjacent levels to a previously fused segment are eligible; non‑adjacent levels are excluded
Documentation required: Operative report of the prior cervical decompression/fusion specifying level(s) and date of surgery
Current cervical spine plain radiographs (AP, lateral, flexion, and extension views) demonstrating successful prior fusion and spinal alignment
MRI and/or CT report of the cervical spine showing neural element compression at the adjacent level with description of the responsible pathology (herniated disc, cyst, stenosis, osteophyte, etc.)
Comprehensive clinical note documenting daily pain severity, functional impairment, radicular pain distribution, and any myelopathic symptoms
Neurological examination note detailing sensory, motor, reflex, and special test findings as required for the indication

Records of conservative management: pharmacy records for ≥6 weeks of prescription analgesics/NSAIDs/steroids/gabapentinoids, physical therapy or chiropractic progress notes for ≥6 weeks, and interventional radiology reports for epidural steroid injections or selective nerve root blocks performed at the same level
Behavioral health evaluation confirming absence of unmanaged mental or substance‑use disorders
Objective cotinine test result (lab report) confirming nicotine‑free status or a signed statement confirming never‑smoker status
